findings.text: The deprecated-path check changed from `obj.(Mock)` to `obj.(*Mock)`. A `Mock` value (`AssertExpectationsForObjects(t, myMock.Mock)`) no longer matches and falls through to `obj.(assertExpectationser)`, which panics because the methods have pointer receivers. A `*Mock` now triggers the deprecation log wrongly.

raw:
Passing a `Mock` by value is now not matched, and `obj.(assertExpectationser)` on a `Mock` value would panic. `Mock` has pointer-receiver methods, so the value doesn't implement the interface. Before this change, a `Mock` value was converted to a pointer and handled. It also now contains a mutex, so copying it triggers a vet error. Passing `*Mock` is the new deprecated path, which is a behavior change: a `*Mock` already satisfied the interface and was never deprecated.
